transcripts.transcript: I would've gone to the careers workshop yesterday, but my lab ran over by nearly an hour.
transcripts.target_signal: would've weak form plus the but-clause reality correction
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Preserve would have as would've; do not produce a spelling-like would of reading. Keep careers workshop and ran over intelligible.

transcripts.transcript: If it weren't for the last bus at ten, I couldn't stay for the evening lab.
transcripts.target_signal: if it weren't for as one conditional unit and couldn't as the hypothetical consequence
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Keep weren't for connected but intelligible; avoid stressing couldn't as if it described the actual situation.

transcripts.transcript: I saved a copy of my interview notes on my phone. Otherwise, I would've had to repeat every interview.
transcripts.target_signal: otherwise followed by the compressed would've had to predicate chain
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: The would-have and had-to boundaries must remain recoverable in natural speech; every interview must remain distinct.

transcripts.transcript: The heater in our dorm has been broken for three weeks. It's time the housing office sent someone to repair it.
transcripts.target_signal: It's time plus past-form sent expressing overdue present action
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Keep It's time and sent clear without an unnatural grammar-teaching pause; pronounce housing office naturally.

transcripts.transcript: Daniel talks as if he'd run the whole clean-up campaign. In fact, he only showed up on the final afternoon, after the other volunteers had done most of the work, yet he makes it sound as though they contributed nothing.
transcripts.target_signal: as if and as though appearance claims contrasted with the In fact correction
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Keep he'd run recoverable as he had run, clean-up clear, and the long factual correction paced without misleading clause boundaries.

transcripts.transcript: The Q&A went smoothly. But for a last-minute practice session with Nina, I might have frozen when they asked about the budget.
transcripts.target_signal: but for as the implicit condition and might have as a non-certain unrealized risk
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Read Q&A as Q and A; keep might have distinct enough to preserve possibility rather than certainty.

transcripts.transcript: You submitted the application before I checked the references, and then you noticed an error. I'd rather you had waited for my feedback.
transcripts.target_signal: I'd rather plus you had waited marking retrospective preference
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: I'd must resolve naturally to I would in context; keep had waited audible and separate from the earlier completed events.

transcripts.transcript: We had hoped to move the lecture indoors before the storm, but the hall was already in use, so the event had to stay outside. If the hall had been available, we'd have moved the audience inside. Without the volunteers quickly covering the equipment, some of it might have been damaged.
transcripts.target_signal: actual hall unavailability, past counterfactual we'd have moved, and might-have-damage risk
transcripts.pronunciation_notes: Maintain clear sentence boundaries in the long script; keep we'd have and might have recoverable without exaggerated teaching stress.
